problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-6$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-6$ | $-2\pi $ | $3\pi $ | $5$ | $-2$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)+2g(x))$ at $x=-6.$

feedback.problem:
The values of functions $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=1$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $q(x)$ | $r(x)$ | ${q}^{′}(x)$ | ${r}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-4$ | $1$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))$ at $x=1.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))|}_{x=1}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))=3{q}^{′}(x)+4{r}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=1$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3q(x)+4r(x))|}_{x=1} & =3{q}^{′}(1)+4{r}^{′}(1) \\  & =3(-4)+4(1) \\  & =-12+4 \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$
